name: Margin Note Drops
subtitle: Pearl drop earrings
description: A single curved line that ends in a pearl — light enough to forget, distinctive enough to be asked about.
material: Hand-finished brass, 22k gold plating, freshwater pearl
dimensions: Drop length 4.2 cm · 3.1 g per earring
care: Keep away from perfume, water and sweat. Wipe with the Nemara cloth after wearing and store in the pouch provided.

images.alt: Margin Note Drops — Pratima's design sketch

idea.body: For twenty-five years Pratima made the same small mark in the margins of her students' notebooks: a curved tick that meant 'yes, this — keep going'. When she began to draw jewellery, it was the first shape her pen made.
idea.note: the tick that meant — keep going.

hand.contribution: Farida casts the curve in brass and hand-files it until the line thins like a pen stroke lifting off the page.

making.body: Cast in small batches in Moradabad, hand-filed, plated in 22k gold and finished with a single freshwater pearl, drilled and set by hand.

moment.body: Monday, 9:40 a.m. The meeting you prepared for. Something small at your ear that says you already know the answer.

name: Monsoon Hour Jhumka
subtitle: Lilac enamel jhumkas
description: A jhumka that heard the rain. Lilac enamel fired in layers, with a fringe that moves a half-second after you do.
material: Brass, 22k gold plating, hand-fired lilac meenakari, glass seed beads
dimensions: Drop length 5.8 cm · 9.4 g per earring
care: Keep away from perfume, water and sweat. Wipe with the Nemara cloth after wearing and store in the pouch provided.

images.alt: Monsoon Hour Jhumka — Pratima's design sketch

idea.body: Pratima remembers sitting on her mother's verandah during the first rain of the monsoon, watching water gather and fall from the edge of the roof. She wanted a jhumka that felt like that moment: a dome, a pause, and then the drop.
idea.note: not ruby. lilac. like the sky just before.

hand.contribution: Meher fires the lilac meenakari in five separate layers — purple is the hardest enamel colour to get right — and sets each bead of the fringe by hand.

making.body: The dome is raised from a single brass sheet, enamelled in Jaipur over three days, plated, and finished with a hand-strung fringe of seed beads.

moment.body: The sangeet, second song. You weren't going to dance. The jhumkas had other plans.

name: Second Glance Hoops
subtitle: Asymmetric filigree hoops
description: One hoop larger than the other, on purpose. The kind of detail people notice the second time they look.
dimensions: Large hoop 4.4 cm · small hoop 2.8 cm · 4.6 g total
care: Store in the pouch to slow tarnishing. Polish gently with the Nemara cloth; avoid chemical dips.

images.alt: Second Glance Hoops — Pratima's design sketch

idea.body: Pratima has never liked things that match too neatly. 'The best students were never symmetrical,' she says. 'They were interesting on one side and surprising on the other.' She drew one hoop, then a smaller one, and refused to correct it.
idea.note: don't fix it. it's better uneven.

hand.contribution: Ramesh twists the silver 'hair' wire into filigree coils and solders over two hundred joins per pair, entirely by eye.

making.body: Each hoop begins as a hand-drawn silver frame, filled with coils of twisted filigree wire in Cuttack, then lightly oxidised so the lace reads in low light.

moment.body: A rooftop at 11 p.m. Someone tilts their head and says, 'Wait — are they different?' Yes. That's the point.

name: The Chalk Line Set
subtitle: Fine collar & studs
description: A fine collar with a single bar, drawn as cleanly as a line of chalk on a blackboard. Comes with matching studs.
dimensions: Collar 38–43 cm adjustable · bar 3.2 cm · studs 0.8 cm
care: Keep away from perfume, water and sweat. Wipe with the Nemara cloth after wearing and store in the pouch provided.

images.alt: The Chalk Line Set — product view
The Chalk Line Set — as worn
The Chalk Line Set — close-up detail
The Chalk Line Set — Pratima's design sketch

idea.body: The first line on a fresh blackboard is the most confident line of the day. Pratima wanted a necklace with that energy — nothing extra, one decision, made well.

hand.contribution: Farida hand-hammers the bar flat, then polishes it so it catches light along one edge only, like chalk on slate.

making.body: The collar wire is drawn and shaped by hand in Moradabad; the bar is hammered, filed and plated, and the matching studs are cut from the same sheet.

moment.body: The presentation. Collar under a crisp shirt. You speak, they listen.

name: Raat Rani Set
subtitle: Filigree collar with violet stones
description: Named for night-blooming jasmine. A filigree collar of petals and violet stones that opens slowly in the dark.
material: 92.5 sterling silver filigree, 22k gold vermeil, violet glass stones
dimensions: Collar 40 cm with 5 cm extender · earrings 3.6 cm
care: Store in the pouch to slow tarnishing. Polish gently with the Nemara cloth; avoid chemical dips.

images.alt: Raat Rani Set — Pratima's design sketch

idea.body: There was a raat rani bush outside the school staff room where Pratima taught. Every evening, after the last bell, its scent arrived before anything else. She drew the petals on the back of an attendance sheet.
idea.note: the flower that only shows up after dark.

hand.contribution: Ramesh builds each petal as a separate filigree cell — the full collar holds over four hundred hand-twisted coils — before it is vermeil-plated and set with violet stones.

making.body: Twenty-one filigree petals are made one by one in Cuttack, linked into a flexible collar, gold-vermeil plated and hand-set with violet stones. A matching pair of petal drops completes the set.

moment.body: A wedding reception, late. Hair up, shoulders bare. Everybody asks where it's from — and then who made it.

name: Inheritance, Rewritten
subtitle: Temple-motif necklace set
description: The temple necklace your grandmother wore — asked a new question. Repoussé discs, spaced like breath, around a single pearl.
material: Brass, 22k gold plating, hand-chased repoussé discs, pearl accents
dimensions: Necklace 44 cm · centre disc 3.4 cm · earrings 3.0 cm
care: Keep away from perfume, water and sweat. Wipe with the Nemara cloth after wearing and store in the pouch provided.

idea.body: Pratima inherited one piece of temple jewellery, too heavy to wear and too precious to change. Instead she asked: what would this look like if it had been designed for my daughter? Fewer discs. More space. The same reverence.
idea.note: keep the prayer, lose the weight.

hand.contribution: Lakshmi presses each disc from behind on a bed of pitch — lamp, lotus, doorway — so the motifs rise softly from the metal.

making.body: Seven discs are hand-chased in Thrissur, each with a different motif, then linked on a fine chain with pearl spacers and plated in 22k gold.

moment.body: Diwali morning at your grandmother's house. She holds the centre disc, turns it over, and nods.

name: Recess Bracelet
subtitle: Beaded brass bracelet
description: Brass and lilac beads in no particular order. The best part of the school day, worn on your wrist.
material: Hand-finished brass beads, lilac glass beads, stretch cord
care: Keep away from perfume, water and sweat. Wipe with the Nemara cloth after wearing and store in the pouch provided.

idea.body: Recess was when Pratima saw who her students really were — the leaders, the jokers, the quiet ones drawing in corners. This bracelet is deliberately unplanned: no two have the same order of beads.

hand.contribution: Farida hand-polishes every brass bead with walnut shell, then strings them by feel rather than by count.

making.body: Brass beads are cast, tumbled and finished by hand in Moradabad, then strung with lilac glass beads in a different sequence every time.

moment.body: Saturday market, coffee in one hand. Stack it with everything or wear it alone.

name: Thread of Thought Cuff
subtitle: Woven filigree cuff
description: An open cuff woven from silver threads — a reminder that every good idea is a few loose ends, pulled together.
dimensions: Opening 2.4 cm · width 1.8 cm · fits most wrists
care: Store in the pouch to slow tarnishing. Polish gently with the Nemara cloth; avoid chemical dips.

images.alt: Thread of Thought Cuff — product view
Thread of Thought Cuff — as worn
Thread of Thought Cuff — close-up detail
Thread of Thought Cuff — Pratima's design sketch

idea.body: Pratima's lesson plans were never linear. They were webs — one idea leading to three more. She wanted a cuff that looked the way her thinking felt: woven, open-ended, holding together because of its threads.

hand.contribution: Ramesh weaves six strands of twisted silver over a frame by hand, then solders the weave at forty points so it holds its shape.

making.body: A silver frame is shaped in Cuttack and filled with a hand-woven lattice of twisted filigree wire, then gently domed so it sits close to the wrist.

moment.body: Thursday evening. Laptop closed, sleeves rolled up. Straight from the office to dinner, no change needed.

name: Lantern Bracelet
subtitle: Enamel link bracelet
description: Small enamel links that glow like lanterns strung across a courtyard on a festival night.
material: Brass, 22k gold plating, hand-fired violet meenakari
dimensions: Length 17.5 cm + 2 cm extender · link 1.1 cm
care: Keep away from perfume, water and sweat. Wipe with the Nemara cloth after wearing and store in the pouch provided.

idea.body: Every Diwali the girls' hostel strung paper lanterns across the courtyard, and Pratima walked beneath them doing the night round. Years later she drew a bracelet that looked like that row of lights.
idea.note: a row of small lights. walking under them.

hand.contribution: Meher enamels each link individually in deep violet and plum, then fires them twice so the colour glows from beneath the surface.

making.body: Eleven links are cut, enamelled and double-fired in Jaipur, then joined by hand with gold-plated jump rings.

moment.body: Festival night on the terrace. Sparklers, laughter, a wrist that catches the light every time you raise a glass.

name: Sunday Kada
subtitle: Hammered brass kada
description: A hammered kada with the slow warmth of a Sunday morning. Irregular, soft, entirely yours.
care: Keep away from perfume, water and sweat. Wipe with the Nemara cloth after wearing and store in the pouch provided.

idea.body: Sundays were the only day Pratima didn't correct anything. This kada is a celebration of the unedited — every hammer mark left exactly where it fell.

hand.contribution: Farida hammers each kada by hand over a steel mandrel — around three hundred blows — and refuses to make two the same.

making.body: Cast brass blanks are hammered by hand in Moradabad, shaped round on a mandrel, plated and finished to a soft satin glow.

moment.body: Sunday, late breakfast, newspaper, nowhere to be. Then Monday, and you leave it on.

name: Aangan Kada
subtitle: Repoussé courtyard kada
description: An aangan — the open courtyard at the heart of a home — pressed into brass and wrapped around the wrist.
care: Keep away from perfume, water and sweat. Wipe with the Nemara cloth after wearing and store in the pouch provided.

idea.body: Pratima grew up in a house built around a courtyard: the place where everyone eventually met. She asked Lakshmi whether a kada could hold a courtyard. Lakshmi said she had one in mind.
idea.note: the room with no roof, where everyone meets.

hand.contribution: Lakshmi presses the courtyard motif — pillars, tulsi, a doorway — from the inside of the band over two days of slow repoussé.

making.body: A brass band is set on pitch in Thrissur and chased from behind, then from the front, until the motif stands in soft relief; it is then plated and hand-burnished.

moment.body: The griha pravesh of your first home. Everyone in the courtyard. You, in the doorway.

name: Ink & Gold Kada Pair
subtitle: Enamel-inlay kada pair
description: Two gold kadas, each drawn through with a single line of purple enamel — Nemara's signature, in ink.
material: Brass, 22k gold plating, hand-fired Nemara-ink enamel
dimensions: Width 0.7 cm each · available in 2.4, 2.6 and 2.8
care: Keep away from perfume, water and sweat. Wipe with the Nemara cloth after wearing and store in the pouch provided.

images.alt: Ink & Gold Kada Pair — product view
Ink & Gold Kada Pair — as worn
Ink & Gold Kada Pair — close-up detail
Ink & Gold Kada Pair — Pratima's design sketch

idea.body: Purple was the colour of Pratima's pen for twenty-five years — she used it instead of red because red felt like a scolding, and purple felt like a conversation. This pair carries that line of ink.
idea.note: purple, not red. a conversation, not a correction.

hand.contribution: Meher cuts a channel into each band and fills it with Nemara-ink enamel, firing it four times until the line is perfectly even.

making.body: Brass bands are channelled, enamelled and fired in Jaipur, then plated in 22k gold so the purple line sits flush with the metal.

moment.body: Any day you want to sign your name on it. Wear them together, or give one away.
